items.cheapest_check: Google's documentation for the Reports API and the audit log export options on Business Standard, read against whatever SIEM or log service the firm would use.
items.unknown: Whether GWS.COMMONCONTROLS.14.1v1 can be met on the Business Standard edition (A1, A5).
items.why: Google's edition documentation puts BigQuery log export outside Business Standard, but the baseline accepts any route that delivers the critical logs to a SIEM; until a route is chosen, GWS.COMMONCONTROLS.14.1v1 is a Gap with an open edition question.

items.cheapest_check: The Admin console's Drive and Docs settings for Drive for desktop, read by the founder.
items.unknown: Whether Drive for desktop's ransomware monitoring is on (D3).
items.why: GWS.DRIVEDOCS.5.2v1 stays Unknown until the setting is read.

items.cheapest_check: The Admin console's Google Meet settings, the meeting-notes section, read by the founder.
items.unknown: The Meet settings for AI-generated meeting notes (E2).
items.why: GWS.MEET.6.1v1, GWS.MEET.6.2v1 and GWS.MEET.6.3v1 stay Unknown until the settings are read.

items.cheapest_check: The founder opens their own Google account's security page and reads the recovery email and phone.
items.unknown: Whether the founder's personal email account is still a recovery address on the super admin account (A4).
items.why: With super admin self-recovery on, a recovery address outside the firm is a second door to the tenant's only super admin account.

items.cheapest_check: Match the client ID against the firm's installed apps and service accounts, and ask the founder and the office manager which vendor set it up.
items.unknown: Which app or vendor holds the domain-wide delegation grant (B5).
items.why: A domain-wide delegation client with Gmail and Drive scopes can read any user's mail and files without their sign-in; GWS.COMMONCONTROLS.10.1v1 cannot be fixed safely until it is identified.
